function: GNN node-pruning policy, trained by imitation learning, accelerates a branch-and-bound global solver for ISAC transmit beamforming (sum rate plus CRB); beamformers still come from convex subproblems (p. 18-23).
system: MIMO ISAC base station, Nt=6 (also 8, 10) transmit and Nr=16 receive antennas, K=3 single-antenna downlink users, extended target; no RIS; band not stated (p. 6, 23, 28).
method: Message-passing GNN (antenna and user nodes) as binary node-pruning classifier, trained by imitation learning (weighted cross-entropy, Adam, 20 epochs) on labels from vanilla B&B (p. 19-21, 26).
data_channel: Custom random instances: Scenario 1 i.i.d. complex Gaussian channels; Scenario 2 Rayleigh fading with path loss 32.6+36.7log10(d) dB, users 50-200 m; no 3GPP model or dataset (p. 23).
test_conditions: GNN trained on randomly generated instances labeled by vanilla B&B; tested on 20 random instances for (K,Nt)=(3,6),(3,8),(3,10) in both scenarios; training problem sizes not stated (p. 21, 28).
baselines: Vanilla B&B (non-learned, same method without GNN) for speed and optimality gap; WMMSE-SDR [31] (non-learned local algorithm) against vanilla B&B only; no other learned method (p. 25-28).
metrics: Optimality gap (Ogap), running-time speedup, sum rate versus CRB, objective value, iteration number, lower and upper bounds (p. 24-28).
complexity: Vanilla B&B: worst-case iteration bound exponential in K (Theorem 2, p. 18); GNN version: measured running-time speedup 3-7x (Table I, p. 28); no GNN operation count.
q1_support: p. 23: "follows the i.i.d. complex Gaussian distribution" (Scenario 1) and "experience Rayleigh fading with a path loss of 32.6 + 36.7 log10 (d) dB" (Scenario 2) - custom channels; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 28: "The results are averaged over 20 random test instances" - same instance distribution; the paper does not state training at another problem size or testing at an unseen scenario or user count (Table I varies Nt only).
q3_support: p. 27: "We define two metrics to compare the vanilla B&B and GNN-based accelerated B&B algorithms" - the only learned method is the proposed GNN, compared with its own non-learned vanilla B&B; no earlier learned method (such as [18], [34], [35]) is compared.
q4_support: p. 18: "grows exponentially fast with the total number of users K" (Theorem 2 iteration bound); p. 28: "can achieve a 3-7 times speedup over the vanilla B&B algorithm" (running time, Table I); no GNN operation count.
q5_support: p. 21: "Randomly generate a problem instance" - instances are simulated; no code or data link and no public dataset is given.
notes: Marginal include on the learned-component check: the learned part is only a GNN node-pruning policy inside a branch-and-bound global solver for ISAC beamforming; beamformers still come from convex subproblems (CVXPY/MOSEK), and the closed-form and B&B parts are classical optimization. Kept because the trained GNN is part of the proposed accelerated algorithm (p. 18-28); reviewer to confirm. Area 5 (ISAC beamforming) over 3. q2=0: Table I varies Nt (6, 8, 10) but the training sizes are not stated.
